definition: A pack's rules worked out for the measures you set — your ceiling height, your opening's width — not the pack's default. A rule used outside the rooms it was calibrated for still gives its figure, marked out of calibration rather than judged.
more: The classical chair rail is the honest case: at a nine-foot ceiling the derivation puts it below the back of a chair, so the pack marks the rule a judgment and says to set the rail from the window sill instead.
basis: Our wording of how a pack's rules are evaluated at a building's own measures, from the pack schema and the grammar layer. schema/proportion-pack.schema.json, derived_rules expression description: "Formula in named variables the engine binds: module, part, ceiling_height, opening_width, storey_height, column_height."; schema/proportion-pack.schema.json, module.default_size_in description: "A sensible default in inches, so the engine can run without being told."; schema/proportion-pack.schema.json, derived_rules calibrated_for description: "Outside it the rule still evaluates and should not be trusted"; docs/proportion.md: "Outside them `in_range` is withheld and `out_of_calibration` published in its place."; docs/proportion.md: "The chair rail is the honest case. The classical derivation puts it at the pedestal cap, and at a 9-foot ceiling that lands at 23 inches, below the back of a chair."; proportions/systems/trim-classical.json notes: "the chair rail rule is marked judgment, the resolution is that the window sill wins".
